messages:
pagerduty-bot: ALERT: high error rate detected on /v1/generate (prod-model-v2, us-west-2). 5xx rate 18% over 5m, latency P95 4.8s. Pager triggered at 1761234567 :rotating_light:
priya (on-call): I’m on it, acked. Can someone grab logs and confirm crash vs timeout?
alex (sre): seeing a bunch of 5xx from gateway -> model-runner pods, looks like segfaults and OOMs mixed. Attaching a quick tail of runner stderr: ```[2026-03-15T18:02:01Z] model-runner[pid=1423] ERROR: process crashed: signal 11 (SIGSEGV)
[2026-03-15T18:02:03Z] model-runner[pid=1534] INFO: evicting KV cache for prefix 0x7f...
[2026-03-15T18:02:04Z] kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 1534 (model-runner) score 987
```
michael (runtime): hmm segfaults at runtime C++ layer when sequence length > 2048, but we recently rolled a quantized kernel update on the 2am deploy. Could be a kernel mismatch with some models.
luis (infra): capacity looks normal, no host-level OOMs. These are per-pod OOM kills. Node memory usage around 68%.
priya (on-call): Jordan from support says two enterprise customers reported request failures and timeouts in the last 10m, CS is escalating. Jordan, any exact endpoints?
jordan (support): search-api and chat-stream endpoint complaints, some clients got 502/504. We have a Slack thread with a customer report, pinged account team.
alex (sre): immediate mitigation ideas: 1) scale up dedicated pool for prod-model-v2 to siphon traffic, 2) rollback the quantized kernel, 3) enable fallback to smaller model variant (prod-model-v2-alt) via routing. Any objections?
michael (runtime): I'd prefer fallback routing first, then rollback if that doesn’t reduce crashes. Fallback avoids touching infra. We have a routing policy ready: route->model_variant: prod-model-v2-alt if error rate > 5%.
priya (on-call): deploy-bot, can you apply the routing override now?
deploy-bot: executing: `redwood route update --route /v1/generate --policy error_threshold=5 --fallback prod-model-v2-alt` — started.
deploy-bot: done. Traffic shift commencing (gradual 30% over 1m).
alex (sre): monitoring logs and metrics now. 30s in and 5xx rate dropped to 10%, still elevated. P95 down to 3.1s.
michael (runtime): I'll start a canary rollback of the quantized kernel on a small subset of runners to confirm. Command: `k rollout undo ds/model-quant-kernels --to-revision=20260314-1 --namespace=prod`
luis (infra): prepping a temporary extra node pool if we need more dedicated capacity. ETA 4-6 minutes to spin up.
priya (on-call): jordan, update customers that we have an automated fallback in place and are investigating root cause; expect intermittent errors to decrease.
jordan (support): on it, posted to customer thread and created incident CPI.
alex (sre): quick debug note — core dumps are being generated at `/var/crash/model-runner.*.core`. Michael, do you want those collected for postmortem?
michael (runtime): yes please. Also try to capture `gdb -c core --batch -ex "bt full"` output. Prioritizing stack traces from signal 11.
luis (infra): running a script to collect cores and `kubectl logs` for the last 5 pods, pushing to /artifacts/incidents/1761234567/ now.
priya (on-call): live mitigation checklist: 1) routing fallback applied (done), 2) rollback canary (michael, in progress), 3) scale dedicated if 5xx > 10% after 5m, 4) customer comms (jordan). Assigning owners.
alex (sre): also toggling aggressive LRU eviction on KV cache to reduce memory pressure: `PATCH /configs/model-runner?kv_lru=true` — applied to canary.
michael (runtime): rollback canary completed on 20% of runners. So far those pods show no SIGSEGV in logs. 5xx rate coming down to 6.2%.
priya (on-call): good. hold open for 10 more minutes, then decide whether to roll rollback global. If stable, we'll keep fallback for 30m and notify customers.
jordan (support): customer update sent: "We detected elevated errors and have shifted traffic to a stable variant; we continue to investigate. We'll provide update in 30 minutes."
alex (sre): ongoing metrics: error-rate timeline: 18% -> 10% (after fallback) -> 6% (after rollback canary). CPU and GPU utilization steady. No node-level OOMs.
michael (runtime): pulling a representative core: stack shows crash in `compact_attention::compute` inside quantized kernel path. Looks reproducible with longer sequences and certain prompt patterns. I’ll open a bug with reproducer and tag kernel owners.
priya (on-call): any quick permanent mitigations? e.g., limit max sequence length per request temporarily?
alex (sre): we could enforce `max_tokens=2048` at the gateway for prod-model-v2 for now, but we already routed to fallback. Might be useful if we revert routing.
luis (infra): extra node pool spun up and standing by, not needed yet.
jordan (support): customers responding, most see significant improvement. One still has errors — digging into request IDs.
priya (on-call): next steps: michael to file runtime bug with triage label and PR for kernel revert; alex to prepare a global rollback plan if needed; luis to stand by for scale; jordan to keep customers updated. We will reconvene 30m or earlier if spikes recur.
michael (runtime): filing bug now: BUG-5712 - segfault in quantized attention kernel with long sequences. Attaching core and gdb output.
alex (sre): logging incident for postmortem with preliminary severity: Sev2 (customer-facing errors but mitigated).
priya (on-call): closing pager for now — monitoring in a calm state but keeping thread open for postmortem notes. If anyone sees a regression, ping me directly. :thumbsup:
pagerduty-bot: Pager resolved at 1761234867 (incident state: acknowledged -> mitigated).
